Risk: Access to patient exports in cloud storage cannot be traced, so a breach cannot be scoped or reported in time
Asset: Patient exports and the cloud storage that holds them
Threat: Insider or attacker reading or copying exports without being noticed
Vulnerability: Storage access logging is off in the s3-secure module; CloudTrail records account activity but not who read individual files (Checkov CKV_AWS_18; Trivy AWS-0089)
Existing controls: CloudTrail trail records account-level activity (tested Day 12, not deployed); no record of who read or copied individual files
Planned controls: Server access logging to a separate log bucket for every patient-data bucket; CloudTrail data events for the patient export bucket; log retention set by the retention schedule in R-017 (target residual: L2 x I3 = 6; Medium)
Linked control (ISO 27001:2022 / NIST CS: ISO A.8.15; A.5.28 / NIST DE.CM; RS.AN

Risk: Patient data is protected only by provider-managed encryption keys, so the company cannot control, rotate or audit who can decrypt it
Asset: Patient data in cloud storage, disks and audit logs
Threat: Compromised cloud identity or over-privileged administrator decrypting data
Vulnerability: No customer-managed encryption keys on buckets, disks or CloudTrail logs (Checkov CKV_AWS_145, CKV_AWS_189, CKV_AWS_35; Trivy AWS-0132, AWS-0027, AWS-0015; Semgrep CMK rules)
Existing controls: Default encryption at rest with provider-managed keys (AES-256) on every bucket; encrypted disks
Planned controls: Customer-managed KMS keys with automatic rotation and a restrictive key policy for patient-data buckets, disks and CloudTrail logs only; provider-managed keys accepted for lower-sensitivity data (target residual: L1 x I4 = 4; Low)

Risk: Cloud console account is taken over because multi-factor sign-in is not enforced by policy
Asset: AWS account and the patient data and logs it holds
Threat: Attacker using a stolen or guessed console password
Vulnerability: Nothing forces MFA for users in the baseline; password reuse history is 5, below the scanner benchmark of 24 (Trivy AWS-0123; Checkov CKV_AWS_13)
Existing controls: MFA present on every console user and the root account (Day 18 evidence report, 10 November 2026: 4 of 4 checks passed); 14-character minimum password; reuse history of 5
Planned controls: IAM policy that denies all actions except MFA setup until the user signs in with MFA, attached to every group; password reuse history of 24; run the Day 18 evidence script monthly and keep each report (target residual: L1 x I5 = 5; Medium)
Linked control (ISO 27001:2022 / NIST CS: ISO A.8.5; A.8.2; A.5.17 / NIST PR.AA

Risk: Patient data is kept longer than needed because storage has no retention or deletion rules
Asset: Patient exports, old versions and logs in cloud storage
Threat: Breach or data access request exposing old data that should already have been deleted
Vulnerability: No lifecycle rule and no approved retention schedule; versioning keeps every old version indefinitely (Checkov CKV2_AWS_61; Arko rated this CRITICAL on Day 16)
Existing controls: None. Versioning is on, so old versions accumulate; retention periods are not yet defined
Planned controls: Retention schedule approved by the Head of Security and Compliance and the DPO for each data class; optional lifecycle variable in the s3-secure module driven by that schedule; quarterly check that the rules exist (target residual: L2 x I2 = 4; Low)
Linked control (ISO 27001:2022 / NIST CS: ISO A.8.10; A.5.33 / NIST PR.DS; GV.PO / UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)

Risk: Suspicious activity in the cloud account is logged but nobody is alerted, so an attack or insider misuse goes unnoticed
Threat: Attacker or insider changing permissions or switching off logging
Vulnerability: Logs go to storage only: no log analysis, alarms or notification (Checkov CKV2_AWS_10, CKV_AWS_252; Trivy AWS-0162)

Linked control (ISO 27001:2022 / NIST CS: ISO A.8.16; A.8.15 / NIST DE.CM; DE.AE
